book.definition: A written or printed work consisting of pages bound along one side.
book.example: He sat in the chair reading an intriguing book.

read.definition: Look at and comprehend the meaning of written or printed matter.
read.example: She likes to read every evening before sleeping.

page.definition: One side of a leaf of something written or printed.

fold.definition: Bend something over on itself so that one part covers another.
fold.example: Fold the sheet carefully in half.

chapter.definition: A main division of a book, typically with a number or title.
chapter.example: The first chapter hooked the reader immediately.

story.definition: An account of imaginary or real people and events told for entertainment.
story.example: The storyteller captivated everyone in the room.

knowledge.definition: Facts, information, and skills acquired through experience or education.
knowledge.example: Books are an infinite fountain of knowledge.

word.definition: A single distinct meaningful element of speech or writing.

light.definition: The natural agent that stimulates sight and makes things visible.
light.example: Warm amber light illuminated the reader screen.

journey.definition: An act of traveling from one place to another or through an adventure.
journey.example: Every novel is an unforgettable journey.

war.definition: A state of armed conflict between different nations or states.
war.example: The Art of War discusses strategic military deception.

peace.definition: Freedom from disturbance; tranquility or harmonious existence.
peace.example: True peace begins with inner serenity.

mind.definition: The element of a person that enables them to be aware of the world and their experiences.
mind.example: Reading expands the horizons of the mind.

courage.definition: The ability to do something that frightens one; bravery.
courage.example: The general showed great courage in difficult circumstances.

freedom.definition: The power or right to act, speak, or think as one wants without hindrance.

world.definition: The earth, together with all of its countries and peoples.
world.example: Brave New World explores a dystopian technological future.

time.definition: The indefinite continued progress of existence and events in the past, present, and future.
time.example: Take your time to savor every chapter.

dream.definition: A series of thoughts, images, and sensations occurring in a person's mind during sleep.
dream.example: Gregor Samsa woke from troubled dreams.

truth.definition: The quality or state of being true, genuine, or in accordance with fact.
truth.example: Literature often reveals profound philosophical truth.

art.definition: The expression or application of human creative skill and imagination.
art.example: Writing is both a craft and an art.
